title: Rollout deadman timer and capacity-gating to prevent cascading rollback failures
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: During a recent model rollout (canary -> staged promotion) a miscombined autoscaler + rollback race caused a cascading rollback that saturated fallback capacity and created multiple 503s for several customer tenants. The immediate root cause was a missing deadman/timeout on canary promotions and a capacity gating rule that did not account for simultaneous rollback traffic.

Impact: ~12 minutes of elevated error rates for 3 dedicated pools, SLA blips for two customers, increased billable compute due to emergency scale-ups. Not a data leak, but operationally disruptive.

Root cause analysis:
- Promotion path allowed simultaneous full-traffic promotion requests without a global concurrency guard.
- Autoscaler reacted to transient health signal noise and initiated scale adjustments while rollbacks were executing, creating transient over-commit and queue saturation.
- Rollback logic retried promotion attempts when gates failed, with no exponential backoff, leading to repeated state flaps.
- No centralized rollout deadman timer to abort an in-progress promotion after a safety window.

Goals:
1) Prevent a single misconfigured rollout from causing cascading rollbacks and capacity storms.
2) Add deterministic, observable safety gates so operators can reason about live promotions.
3) Build low-touch automation that favors quick safe fallbacks (circuit-breaker behavior) over repeated roll attempts.

Proposed design (high level):
- Introduce a rollout deadman timer (configurable per project) that marks a promotion as "timed_out" if it hasn't reached steady-state within X minutes; timed_out promotions must require manual resume or owner approval to continue.
- Add a global rollout concurrency limit per-cluster and per-customer to prevent multiple simultaneous promotions affecting shared capacity.
- Capacity gating: before a promotion completes, check projected QPS and instance headroom across downstream pools; if projected headroom < threshold, automatically pause promotion and move to a safe_hold state.
- Backoff and circuit-breaker for rollback/promotion retries: exponential backoff with jitter and an escalation path to human review if retries exceed Y attempts.
- Observability and alerts: add a dedicated dashboard for promotion lifecycle (requests, success rate, time to steady state), and a critical alert when a promotion hits deadman or triggers capacity gate.
- Runbook additions: explicit operator steps for timed_out promotions, escalation list, and a quick revert command that performs non-blocking fallback to the previous stable model.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change the autoscaler's core scaling algorithm; it adds guardrails and integration points.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deadman timer implemented and configurable (default 10m) and can be overridden per project.
- Global concurrency limit enforced with telemetry.
- Capacity gating check added to promotion completion path with unit + integration tests.
- Backoff logic added to promotion retry path.
- Dashboard tile and at least one alert rule created.
- Runbook updated and reviewed by SRE and PM.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Tight default thresholds risk increasing manual intervention; choose conservative defaults and iterate.
- Additional checks add latency to promotions; test and measure end-to-end promotion time impact.

Related artifacts:
- Postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/postmortems/2026-02-08-rollout-cascade
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/design/rollout-deadman-capacity-gates
- Dashboard (prototype): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/rollout-lifecycle
- Incident timeline & logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/app/rollouts/incident/2026-02-08

Estimated implementation plan (phases):
1) Spec + API changes for rollout state machine and deadman timer (2w)
2) Implement deadman + concurrency guard + basic capacity check (3w)
3) Backoff/circuit-breaker + tests + dashboard (2w)
4) Staged rollout to canary customers + monitoring + runbook sign-off (1w)
comments: 2026-02-11 - Initial postmortem posted and this follow-up ticket created by Sofia Martinez. Assigned to Maya Chen for implementation. Links to Confluence and dashboard included.
2026-02-15 - Engineering triage: agreed on deadman timer, capacity gating, and retry backoff as primary mitigations. PM (Arjun Patel) requested conservative defaults to minimize operational toil.

2026-02-20 - Design doc draft shared: https://confluence.redwood.ai/design/rollout-deadman-capacity-gates. Requesting SRE review for integration with existing autoscaler signals.
Reviewer: Liam O'Connor - noted we should surface nozzle-level headroom not just cluster-level.

2026-02-25 - SRE feedback incorporated; added per-customer headroom check and cache of recent promotion decisions to avoid thundering herd.
Action: create ENG-74892 to implement headroom estimator service.

2026-03-03 - Prototype deadman timer landed on branch: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/6218. Code owner review requested from @maya.
PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/6218
2026-03-08 - Integration test failure: promotion state not persisted across control-plane failover. Root cause: write path race in rollout-statestore. Created ENG-74893 to harden statestore writes.
2026-03-12 - Manual safety review with PM and SRE complete. Adjusted default deadman to 12m and concurrency default to 1 per-cluster. Moving ticket to In Progress for full implementation.
2026-03-12 - Next steps: finish capacity gating implementation, add alert rule, complete PRs, and schedule canary with 2 non-prod tenants.
